guidanceComparisons.claim: A 20-slide story teaches four prevention habits: cover coughs with the elbow, wash hands with soap and water, keep distance from people outside the home, and stay home when ill. It bridges into the handwashing coach and the cough check.
guidanceComparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: the source book is CC0 and the narrative moved to the phrase bank unchanged in meaning, but it carries 2020 pandemic-era advice, including the two-metre rule. A clinical reviewer must confirm the prevention wording against current local guidance, and the story must never route a danger sign.

guidanceComparisons.claim: A 16-slide day-in-the-life story poses a habit choice at six points and then shows the safer answer: soap before eating, soap after the toilet, sneeze into the elbow, mask before going out, distance at the shop, and handwashing on returning home.
guidanceComparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: the source is a Philippines classroom deck whose licence line is absent, so a rights reviewer must clear reuse before release. The branching source became a linear slideshow; face shields and the two-metre rule need a clinical reviewer against current local guidance.

guidanceComparisons.claim: An eight-beat read-aloud participation story where children act out the cues, reinforcing handwashing with soap on returning home and before eating, and coughing into the elbow.
guidanceComparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: a read-aloud script with no clinical claim beyond soap and elbow habits. A local reviewer should confirm the participation cues suit the setting, and a rights reviewer should confirm the licence line.

guidanceComparisons.claim: A three-frame comic in which the baby asks for more beans and vegetables, used to prompt an antenatal nutrition conversation at a scheduled visit.
guidanceComparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: the closing line, that mother eats for both of us, is faithful to the author's script but is not how current antenatal nutrition guidance is framed - the recommendation is an adequate diet with iron and folate supplementation, and "eating for two" is commonly cited as encouraging excess intake. A clinician must decide whether the line ships as written, reworded, or the frame is dropped. The source art is the author's own placeholder, which his first page asks to have redrawn, and reuse terms inside NurseAunty are unconfirmed. Held out of the caregiver catalogue meanwhile. See docs/reviews/APPROVAL-NOTES.md.

guidanceComparisons.claim: A three-frame comic in which a worm arrives to share the baby's food and the baby asks mother to collect deworming tablets at the clinic.
guidanceComparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: the story routes to a clinic and names no drug, dose or schedule, which matches the project's classify-and-route rule. But preventive deworming in pregnancy is trimester-dependent and endemicity-dependent, so the referral is not universally appropriate and a clinician must confirm it for the target settings, including whether the copy needs a trimester condition. The worm illustration is redrawn for this adaptation; the rest of the art is the author's placeholder. Held out of the caregiver catalogue meanwhile. See docs/reviews/APPROVAL-NOTES.md.
